@graph.name: WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy (WCB) at 19+ Clinics | Synergy Rehab
@graph.description: Hurt at work in BC? Book a WCB physiotherapy assessment at one of 19+ Synergy Rehab clinics from Vancouver to Abbotsford. How claims, visits and costs work.

mainEntity.name: Is WCB the same as WorkSafeBC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. WorkSafeBC is the Workers’ Compensation Board of British Columbia, which is why many people still call it WCB. You will see both names on our booking pages.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a claim number before I book?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. At a WorkSafeBC-contracted physiotherapist you can have your initial assessment before WorkSafeBC accepts your claim. You do need to report the injury to WorkSafeBC so there is a claim to bill, even if it is still pending. WorkSafeBC mails you an 8-digit claim number once it gets your report. Bring it to a later visit if you do not have it yet.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a doctor’s referral for WorkSafeBC physio?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. WorkSafeBC’s guidance for workers is to visit a contracted physiotherapist and explain that the injury is work-related. A doctor’s referral is not one of the steps. Massage therapy is different: it needs a doctor’s referral and an accepted claim.

mainEntity.name: Will I have to pay anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once WorkSafeBC accepts your claim, your provider bills WorkSafeBC for care related to your claim and you should not have to pay any fees. If you have treatment before your claim is accepted, a clinic may ask you to pay, and you can ask for a refund if the claim is accepted later. Ask the clinic how it handles visits while your claim is pending before you book follow-up visits.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my claim is denied?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your claim was pending at your first visit, WorkSafeBC still pays the contracted clinic for that initial assessment, even if the claim is later denied. WorkSafeBC does not pay for treatment visits given while the claim was pending if it is denied.

mainEntity.name: It has been more than 60 days since my injury. Can I still get physio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but WorkSafeBC has to approve treatment first when it starts more than 60 days after the injury. It is not refused automatically. Call the clinic and we will tell you what we need to ask WorkSafeBC.

mainEntity.name: How many physio visits does WorkSafeBC cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: WorkSafeBC sets the length of each treatment period for your claim. If you need more treatment, your physiotherapist can ask WorkSafeBC for it, and WorkSafeBC decides. We explain what is approved for your claim at each stage.

mainEntity.name: What if I go to a physio who is not contracted with WorkSafeBC?

acceptedAnswer.text: You pay for each visit yourself and ask WorkSafeBC to reimburse you at its set rate, which is $95 per visit from April 1, 2026. You pay any difference.

mainEntity.name: Can I get massage therapy on my WorkSafeBC claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a doctor’s referral and an accepted claim. WorkSafeBC covers an assessment and up to 6 massage treatments in the first 8 weeks after the injury without pre-approval. More needs approval. See the clinic list below for clinics that book WCB massage online.

mainEntity.name: How do I report a workplace injury to WorkSafeBC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell your employer as soon as it is safe, and tell anyone who treats you that it happened at work. Then report it to WorkSafeBC online at any time, or by phone through Teleclaim. Teleclaim is 1.888.967.5377 toll-free or 604.231.8888 in the Lower Mainland, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. You have up to one year to report, but report right away.
